note: Byte-level record of the two primary texts this night downloaded and read offline. extract.py turns them into the .txt beside them with nothing but zlib, so the reading is reproducible from these bytes.

files.what: Susan Leigh Star, 'The Ethnography of Infrastructure', American Behavioral Scientist 43(3), 1999, 377-391. Course-hosted copy at UC Irvine.
files.why_this_night_needs_it: The primary text. Its dimension 'Built on an installed base' is the sentence this line has been paraphrasing for three days without knowing whose it was. Read in full; the eight dimensions were read verbatim off p.381-382.

files.what: Paul A. David, 'Clio and the Economics of QWERTY', American Economic Review 75(2), 1985, 332-337. Course-hosted copy at UC Santa Barbara.
files.why_this_night_needs_it: The economics half. S57's replacement claim is the switching-cost account of lock-in; this is where it was named, forty-one years earlier.

fetched_but_deliberately_not_committed.why_not_committed: House rule: the catalogues are feeds, not copies. Mirroring one here creates a second catalogue that drifts from the first. The query and its result are recorded in work.md; the file is not kept.
Same rule. Recorded: the instruction of 2026-08-13 says 1,106 entries and tonight's fetch returned 1,128, which is what a feed does and a copy would not.
